x: Clark raced away at the start and at Beverley Brook was already making the handicapper feel nervous, for so early in the race he had set up a good lead, being followed by H Cook, Bicknell of Thames Valley and Browning of Ashcombe Footer and Klophin being in close attendance.
Cohen had set up a very fast pace, but he was soon caught and passed by Bicknell. Pyer was third, some distance behind, but well ahead of the rest of the field.

Going up the Horse-Ride, Bicknell (T.V.H.) and Penny (Belgrave) put in some good running and got into the first 6 places. Except for a new T.V.H. member in Porter, who made a good effort across the common home, the other positions remained unaltered

Nearing the brook Footer moved up with Nuti and Bicknell of Thames Valley just in front of them. After crossing the bridge the long drag up the "Toast-rack" commenced and it was here that Flower and Allum overtook Cohen.
Bicknell was the first "Valley" man to finish (9th); but as the Bels. placed their fifteen to score in the first 18 positions, we ran out very easy winners of the race.

A word of praise to our lesser lights: Allen, Bicknell, Yorwarth, Laurie, Spooner, Wattam and Willis for their efforts. Also, many thanks to the willing band of cyclists who did yeoman work as attendants.
